rationale: The literature does not support the hypothesis that cerebellar atrophy severity correlates predictably with disease duration, nor that patients imaged within 5 years reliably show absent or minimal atrophy while moderate-to-severe atrophy only appears after 10 to 15 years. Current human clinical reports (Torella et al., 2023; Benkirane et al., 2024; OMIM #621226) document variable presence of cerebellar atrophy (e.g., detected in 7 of 11 cases in Benkirane et al., and absent or slight in several patients in Torella et al.), but do not establish a duration-dependent linear correlation or temporal cutoffs of 5 versus 10-15 years.

evidence.text: Brain imaging was evaluated in 11 cases with TUBA4A variants presenting with ataxia and/or spasticity, revealing cerebellar atrophy in 7 individuals, demonstrating marked inter-individual imaging heterogeneity without an established duration-dependent correlation.

evidence.text: In two families carrying the p.Glu415Lys mutation in TUBA4A presenting with spastic ataxia, brain MRI showed slight or absent cerebellar atrophy across affected individuals rather than consistent progression to moderate-to-severe pancerebellar atrophy.

source.title: A new genetic cause of spastic ataxia: the p.Glu415Lys variant in TUBA4A
source.quote: MRI showed slight or absent cerebellar atrophy.

evidence.text: In dominant Tuba4a Q176P mutant mice, animals appear normal at 3 weeks but develop rapid Purkinje neuron degeneration and severe ataxia between days 22 and 30, demonstrating rapid cellular neurodegeneration rather than a protracted multi-year delay.

source.title: A mouse model of autosomal dominant spastic ataxia and myopathy caused by a mutation in Tuba4a
source.quote: Tuba4a Q176P mice have profound ataxia with Purkinje neuron degeneration beginning between 22 and 30 days.

new_directions.question_text: Does quantitative volumetric MRI of the cerebellum correlate longitudinally with disease duration in prospective TUBA4A SPAX11 cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Current evidence relies on semi-quantitative or qualitative descriptions (atrophy present in 7/11, or slight/absent). Formal voxel-based morphometry is required to test true duration-dependent atrophy kinetics.

new_directions.question_text: Do specific TUBA4A variant alleles (e.g., p.Glu415Lys vs de novo missense alleles) dictate the presence and severity of cerebellar atrophy independently of disease duration?
new_directions.rationale: Different variants may exhibit distinct pathogenic effects on microtubule stability and dynamics, which could explain the variability in cerebellar atrophy across kindreds.
